messages:
mario: FYI - after the runtime rollout (fp8 kernels) we're getting sporadic NaNs on long-prefix chat loads. Tail latency also spiked around the same time. logs show `inf`/`nan` in attention outputs.
ada: saw the same on canary this morning. rolled a quick int8 fallback for affected shard and NaNs stopped. throughput dropped ~3-5% but stable.
ops-bot: deploy rollback: runtime/fp8-2026-03-15 -> rolled back 1712345000 by @ada :done: 
lexi: profiling dump attached (excerpt):
```
kernel_select: fp8_matmul_v2 (seq_len=4096, batch=4)
matmul_fp8_v2: peak_s8=127, scale=12.3 -> overflow detected
layernorm_fp8: rescale applied=2.5e-4
kv_cache_write: avg_write_us=0.8
```
lexi: looks like the selector picks fp8_matmul_v2 for large seqs which pushes the per-op scale high and we overflow on a few heads. smoothquant seems to amplify the issue on embed and first attention layers.
sam: quick mitigation tested locally: set ENV `FP8_MAX_SCALE=8.0` and enable KV rescale path `KV_RESCALE_MODE=per_request`. also disabled smoothquant for layers [0,1]. command used: `./run_canary --env FP8_MAX_SCALE=8.0 --env KV_RESCALE_MODE=per_request --disable-smoothquant=0,1`
ada: after that config on canary (1000 long-prefix requests) -> 0 NaNs, tail latency slightly worse (~+12ms) but no crash. throughput -4%.
mario: proposed next steps:
- add NaN telemetry counters (layer id, kernel name, seq_len, batch)
- implement automatic fallback: if NaN seen -> re-run request on int8 kernel and increment metric
- tweak kernel selector: prefer int8 when avg_seq>1024 or batch>6 for fp8-capable models
- sweep FP8_MAX_SCALE default (8/10/12) with perf+quality evals
lexi: +1. also recommend a clamp in smoothquant per-channel scale: from `max(scale, 1e-3)` to `clamp(scale, 1e-3, 10.0)` to avoid runaway scales.
sam: I'll open a PR to add the fallback and telemetry. note: fallback adds ~30ms p95 for those rare cases, but better than NaN.
ops-bot: created INF-1423: "FP8 NaN spike on long-prefix workloads - telemetry + fallback" assigned to @sam, @lexi.
ad a: typo -> ada: we should also add a unit test that injects an artificially large scale to confirm fallback triggers.
mario: agree. scheduling a quick perf run after PR merges. If perf hit is acceptable we'll roll fp8 back forward with the new guards.
lexi: small note for kernel-selector: prefer `int8_matmul_v1` for dense matmul when batch>8 and seq>512, because it keeps scales bounded and is faster than fp8 under those workload shapes (we measured this in last quarter).
sam: opened PR #2046: runtime: add fp8_nan_telemetry + auto_fallback_to_int8 + FP8_MAX_SCALE env (w/ default=8.0). test plan in PR description.
mario: thanks team. next sync: confirm perf run (full convo replay) and then decide rollout window. :thumbsup:
